$doc: Profile's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component profile` block in css/components.css and of dist/react/profile.tsx. Same contract as components/button/definition.json: a plain string is a structural literal, {"token": "x"} binds --x, and an array is a sequence of both. PROFILE IS THE OTHER BLOCK THAT FORCED THE ORDERED LIST, and its case is the mirror of media's: `.profile > div:nth-child(odd)` is written at the FOOT, after every part, beside the query that undoes it — because the right-hand gutter and its removal at one column are one thought, and a fixed cascade would have emitted the position directly under the rule it qualifies, three rules earlier. It also forced `child`. `.profile > div` has to be a child: the markup wraps each dt/dd pair in a <div> so the grid has a row to place, and a descendant selector would style a <div> nested anywhere inside a value. The closure that keeps that from being the wedge PATTERNS.md refuses is written in the schema and enforced by the build — a child combinator may only reach a BARE TAG, and a class may only be reached by a descendant — so `.profile > div` is sayable and `.band > .rail--l` is not.

rules.$doc: A <dl> laid out as two columns of pairs. The type is mono and small because this is a scannable index of facts rather than prose — the same voice a fact title or a chip uses, at the step above the floor.

rules.name: pair
rules.$doc: One label-and-value pair, which the markup wraps in a <div> so that the outer grid has a single box to place. It is a grid of its own — a fixed label track and a fluid value — so every label in both columns lines up on the same edge. A CHILD and not a descendant: a <div> inside a value is content, not a row, and a descendant selector would lay it out as one.

rules.name: term
rules.$doc: The label. Uppercase mono at the label ink — the chrome voice, so the value beside it reads as the content and the term as its heading.

rules.name: value
rules.$doc: The fact itself, at body ink. One declaration, and the <dd>'s own margin is already off in the foundation reset.

rules.name: ok
rules.$doc: A positive status value — one per list, and spec.md is where that rule lives because it is about markup rather than appearance. `.is-ok` is a state class the page owns rather than this component, which is why it is a scoped part on a foreign class: the profile decides what an affirmative value looks like inside it, and does not decide what is affirmative.

rules.name: left-column
rules.$doc: The gutter between the two columns, put on the left-hand pairs rather than in the grid's own `gap`, so that the border-bottom of every pair runs the full width of its column and the two columns of rules read as one ruled table. It is the first `odd` in the position vocabulary, and the first member of it that names a SET of siblings rather than one.

One column. The gutter goes with the second column it was separating — the same two facts as above, stated the other way round, which is what makes this an override of named rules rather than a second layout.
